reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive deficiency of short/branched-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (ACADSB gene), an enzyme in the catabolism of the branched-chain amino acid isoleucine
Most individuals identified by newborn screening are asymptomatic, and the condition is generally regarded as a mostly benign biochemical phenotype
It is notably frequent in the Hmong population, in whom it is often clinically silent
When symptoms occur they are non-specific and may include hypotonia, lethargy, feeding difficulties or, rarely, metabolic decompensation during illness
Newborn screening detects raised C5 (2-methylbutyrylcarnitine), which overlaps with isovaleric acidaemia and requires confirmatory testing
Urine organic acids show 2-methylbutyrylglycine, confirming the isoleucine-pathway defect
Management, where any is needed, is supportive with avoidance of prolonged fasting and an emergency regimen providing glucose during catabolic illness
reference.pathophysiology: Short/branched-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (SBCAD), encoded by ACADSB, catalyses the dehydrogenation of 2-methylbutyryl-CoA in the mitochondrial catabolic pathway of isoleucine. When the enzyme is deficient, 2-methylbutyryl-CoA accumulates and is conjugated to glycine and carnitine, appearing as 2-methylbutyrylglycine in urine and raised 2-methylbutyrylcarnitine (C5) in blood. The metabolic block is usually well tolerated, and most affected individuals remain healthy; only occasionally, and typically under catabolic stress, do non-specific symptoms or mild decompensation arise. Because C5 elevation overlaps with isovaleric acidaemia, biochemical distinction is important.
additionalDifferentials: Isovaleric acidaemia (the main C5 elevation to distinguish)
Multiple acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (glutaric aciduria type II)
Benign biochemical variants detected on screening
Non-metabolic causes of neonatal hypotonia and lethargy
additionalInvestigations: Plasma acylcarnitine profile showing elevated C5 (2-methylbutyrylcarnitine)
Plasma free and total carnitine to detect secondary deficiency
Blood glucose, blood gas and ammonia during any symptomatic episode
ACADSB molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Differentiating tests to exclude isovaleric acidaemia when C5 is raised
redFlags: Metabolic decompensation with hypoglycaemia or acidosis during intercurrent illness
Significant lethargy, poor feeding or encephalopathy in a symptomatic infant
Failure to thrive or neurodevelopmental concern
reference.prognosis: The disorder is generally benign, with most individuals identified by screening remaining asymptomatic and developing normally; rare symptomatic cases have a good outcome with avoidance of fasting and supportive care during illness.
pitfalls: Confusing the C5 elevation with isovaleric acidaemia and mismanaging accordingly
Over-treating an asymptomatic screen-positive child as though significant disease is present
Failing to confirm the diagnosis with urine organic acids and molecular testing
Overlooking secondary carnitine deficiency during follow-up
references: Scriver's OMMBID: Disorders of Isoleucine Metabolism
Saudubray, Baumgartner & Walter, Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment
management: Reassurance and observation, as most individuals identified by newborn screening are asymptomatic and need no specific treatment
Avoid prolonged fasting and provide prompt carbohydrate and energy intake during intercurrent illness to prevent catabolic decompensation
Consider carnitine supplementation where secondary carnitine deficiency is documented
Treat the rare metabolic decompensation with intravenous glucose during illness, monitoring glucose, blood gas and ammonia
Confirm the diagnosis and distinguish it from isovaleric acidaemia after a raised C5 acylcarnitine on newborn screening
Provide metabolic dietetic input and a written emergency regimen for illness
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance, noting the high carrier frequency in the Hmong population
